label: rem:glossary-weierstrass-projection
title: Weierstrass projection $\wp_q(z)$
html:
Definition. Let \mathcal{E}_q be the Descartes elliptic curve with Weierstrass coefficients p(q), r(q), and let \Lambda_q \subset \mathbb{C} be the period lattice of \mathcal{E}_q. The Weierstrass projection is the meromorphic function \wp_q : \mathbb{C}/\Lambda_q \to \mathbb{P}^1 defined by

  \wp_q(z) =  \frac{1}{z^2}
  +  \sum_{\omega \in \Lambda_q \setminus \{0\}}
  \left(\frac{1}{(z - \omega)^2} - \frac{1}{\omega^2}\right).

Period lattice. The lattice \Lambda_q is spanned by the two fundamental periods \omega_1(q), \omega_2(q) obtained by integrating the holomorphic differential \mathrm{d}x / y over a basis of H_1(\mathcal{E}_q, \mathbb{Z}). The lattice modulus \tau_q = \omega_2(q)/\omega_1(q) satisfies \mathrm{Im}(\tau_q) > 0 and encodes the conformal class of \mathcal{E}_q.

Uniformisation. The map

  \mathbb{C}/\Lambda_q \xrightarrow{ \sim } \mathcal{E}_q,
  \qquad
  z  \longmapsto  [\wp_q(z) : \wp_q'(z) : 1]

is an isomorphism of Riemann surfaces. This exhibits \mathbb{C}/\Lambda_q as the universal cover of \mathcal{E}_q.

Differential equation. The function \wp_q satisfies

  \wp_q'(z)^2 =  4\wp_q(z)^3
  +  4p(q)\wp_q(z)
  +  4r(q),

which is the standard Weierstrass equation \wp'^2 = 4\wp^3 - g_2\wp - g_3 with invariants g_2(q) = -4p(q) and g_3(q) = -4r(q). The factor of 4 converts the short Weierstrass form to the classical \wp-function normalisation.

Regime table.

Regime q Lattice shape Physics
Classical q = 1 \Lambda_1 rectangular Degenerate curve \mathcal{E}_1; no crossing asymmetry
Physical substrate q \Lambda_q rhombic Our universe; \mathcal{E}_q smooth, \Delta < 0
Deep quantum q \to \infty \Lambda_q \to hexagonal CM lattice; maximal symmetry

Notation convention. We reserve the symbol \wp for the Weierstrass elliptic function associated to \mathcal{E}_q. We never repurpose it. We write \wp(z) for \wp_q(z) when the dependence on q is clear.
